card.title: Ki-30 ANN
card.text: When this unit attacks, deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card.flavorText: The Mitsubishi Ki-30, known to the Allies as the "Ann", was a Japanese light bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. Developed in the late 1930s, the Ki-30 was a monoplane with a single engine, featuring an enclosed cockpit, fixed landing gear, and a crew of two (pilot and observer/gunner). It was designed to be fast and maneuverable, capable of carrying small bomb loads for close air support and tactical bombing missions. The Ki-30 first saw combat during the Second Sino-Japanese War, where it proved effective in low-altitude bombing against Chinese forces. It was well-regarded early on for its simplicity, reliability, and ability to operate from rough airfields. However, by the time the Pacific War began, the Ki-30 was becoming obsolete due to its limited speed, range, and payload capacity compared to newer aircraft. It saw service during the early stages of the war in Southeast Asia, but was gradually phased out from frontline roles by 1942. The Ki-30 could not match the performance of more modern Allied fighters and bombers and was therefore relegated to training and secondary duties. A few surviving planes were also used as kamikaze aircraft later in the war. Despite this, the aircraft played an important role in Japan's early air campaigns and contributed to the initial wave of Japanese successes in Asia.
